title: A public comment route can exist while participation and agency learning remain uneven
source_unit: U.S. Government Accountability Office GAO-26-108115 review of Treasury and IRS tax rulemaking, economic analysis, and taxpayer engagement
geography: United States Treasury and Internal Revenue Service rulemaking

denominator.unit: Treasury and IRS rulemaking activity reviewed by GAO

economically_significant_regulations.unit: regulations designated economically significant in the period

observations.method: GAO quantitative review of tax regulations, review of four selected economic analyses, random sample of 10 proposed regulations, and comparison of public engagement procedures with leading practices.
observations.uncertainty: Counts describe the reviewed rulemaking universe, while the detailed economic-analysis and engagement findings come from selected samples; the report does not provide a national representation or influence estimate.
observations.subgroup: Treasury and IRS rulemaking officials, public commenters, hearing participants, and taxpayers as the affected public; individual participation characteristics are not fully observed.
observations.counterinterpretation: A formal comment route can still provide meaningful input for some rules even when hearing access, documentation, and analytical practices are uneven.

observations.period: 2017-2026; random sample of 10 proposed tax regulations

denominator.unit: proposed regulations randomly selected by GAO from 231 proposed regulations

notice_and_comment.unit: sampled proposed regulations with notice-and-comment procedures

hearing_virtual_access.value: dial-in rather than broadly available video conferencing

observations.method: GAO random sample of proposed regulations and review of notice, comment, and hearing procedures.
observations.uncertainty: The sample does not show who participated, who could not participate, the substance or representativeness of comments, or whether any comment changed a final rule.
observations.subgroup: Public commenters and hearing participants in the selected rulemaking sample.
observations.counterinterpretation: A 61.5-day formal period and comment opportunity can provide a real avenue for input; access and documentation weaknesses do not prove that no public influence occurred.

observations.period: 2017-2026; four selected economically significant tax regulations

denominator.unit: selected final regulations reviewed against OMB economic-analysis practices

summary_accounting_statement.value: not addressed for the four reviewed regulations

observations.method: GAO comparison of four selected final tax regulations with OMB Circular A-4 recommended economic-analysis practices.
observations.uncertainty: The four cases were selected for relevance and are not a representative sample; analytical practice does not itself establish which regulatory design was socially or fiscally best.
observations.subgroup: Economically significant Treasury and IRS regulations reviewed by GAO.
observations.counterinterpretation: Consistent analysis of alternatives can improve regulatory design even when cost, benefit, and revenue estimates are incomplete.

denominator.unit: GAO oversight assessment of Treasury and IRS preparedness for emerging comment-volume and AI-writing conditions

mass_comment_policy.unit: policy for identifying and documenting mass comments, including AI-assisted comments

administrative_challenge.value: near-duplicate comments can be harder to identify
administrative_challenge.unit: reported consequence of AI-assisted comment generation

recommendations.unit: GAO recommendations to improve analysis, comment handling, virtual participation, and documentation

observations.method: GAO review of rulemaking procedures and emerging technology implications.
observations.uncertainty: The report does not measure the prevalence of AI-generated comments, distinguish genuine independent views from coordinated submissions, or show how agencies would respond in a particular rule.
observations.subgroup: Treasury and IRS rulemaking administrators and members of the public submitting comments.
observations.counterinterpretation: AI can lower participation costs and enable more people to express a view; the administrative problem is how to preserve meaningful representation while processing scale.

related_sources.claim: GAO's product page provides report metadata and recommendation status.

boundary: This record measures formal rulemaking opportunity, selected comment and hearing conditions, economic-analysis practices, and AI/mass-comment preparedness. It does not establish public representation, comment influence on final rules, taxpayer burden or benefit, trust change, or political legitimacy.
